node.title: Re: Clearing a hash reference
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Please try to reduce your code down to the minimum needed to reproduce the issue - see [id://1177642|SSCCE]. Like this:

use warnings; use strict; use Data::Dump; { package Foo; use Moose; has 'Fields' => (is => 'rw', isa => 'HashRef'); } my $foo = Foo->new(Fields=>{}); $foo->Fields->{x}++; dd $foo->Fields; # prints { x => 1 } #$foo->Fields = 0; # wrong, fails $foo->Fields({}); dd $foo->Fields; # prints {}

The problem is that $foo->Fields is a method call, to which you cannot assign anything ($foo->Fields = ...;) by default; it's as if you had written sin($pi) = 123;. The normal way to set an object property is to pass its new value as an argument to the method, as I showed above: $foo->Fields({});

There is a way to make methods that you can assign to in Perl, [doc://perlsub#Lvalue-subroutines], but at least in my experience they seem to be pretty uncommon. I suggest you stick to normal setter calls.

Also, let me repeat [Mr. Muskrat]'s [id://1201467|suggestion] to look into [mod://DBIx::Class] instead of reinventing that wheel.
